The contempt hearings, if finally allowed, will shed light on any contempt by DOJ, and may turn up evidence related to Bove’s confirmation. This has been too long, riddled with seeming judicial obstruction by Trump judges (read the dissents!).

Along the way, I asked the Chief Judge to make sure there was no coordination between the Trump judges behind the exceptionally long administrative stay and the MAGA DOJ jamming Bove through confirmation in that window. No evidence that was done.
That won’t happen until at least the fall, but after then, Boasberg may at last be cleared to proceed with the hearing that should have been held BEFORE thug Bove’s jammed-through confirmation.

After *another* four months, the two Trump judges tried (again) to shut down Judge Boasberg’s inquiry for good. (Read the dissent!)

Now the circuit court has thrown out that second ruling and will decide what happens next, en banc.

The circuit en banc effectively threw out that ruling, and Judge Boasberg was explicitly told he could go ahead with the contempt proceedings. When he gave notice, MAGA DOJ got another administrative stay from two Trump judges.
Finally, after months of sitting on their hands, the Trump judges issued a ruling to try to shut down Judge Boasberg permanently. (Read the dissent!)

In those four months, DOJ and Senate Republicans shoved Bove through his confirmation process to become an appellate judge. 

No Republican said “not til the contempt findings are made.”

MAGA DOJ was not happy, and suddenly two Trump appointees ordered an “administrative stay” of the contempt proceedings.  

Administrative stays usually last only days or weeks; this one lasted four months.
DOJ’s noncompliance caused the judge to open an inquiry into possible contempt of court. In that contempt proceeding, Emil Bove might have had to testify, and his conduct would have been scrutinized.
